subject: Any way to do a "reverse" procD.lm

messages.author: bc3244d9806438a2
messages.subject: Any way to do a "reverse" procD.lm
parts:
In geomorph, is there a way to use procD.lm or advanced.procD.lm such that shape is an independent variable. I’m used to doing this:

 

procD.lm(coords ~ species + force) #shape as a function of species and force needed to crush

but I really need

procD.lm(force ~ coords + species) #crushing force as a function of shape and species

 

When I try I get a type mismatch, even when using a dataframe. I can do it in other stats software (e.g. PAST) but with shape as each x and y coordinate, which is impossible to interpret in a meaningful way.

 

Thanks!

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Any way to do a "reverse" procD.lm
parts:
Russel,

Did you convert coords to a matrix?  As a dependent variable, we do that in the procD.lm function but we do not try to catch 3D arrays as variables for the independent variables, because as you say for other programs, they usually are one by one, single vectors.

Try,

X <- two.d.array(coords)

and then use X in place of coords in your second function.

Now whether you should be doing this or how to interpret it are different issues.  I would posit that the coefficients of your model will have no appreciable meaning, but the collective variance explained might be useful to know.

Mike
